zebralogic.title: Assign fixed‑position attributes immediately
zebralogic.principle: When a clue directly states that a specific attribute value belongs to a particular house number, place that value in that house right away. This reduces the search space and prevents later contradictions.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue mentions a house index (e.g., 'first house', 'third house') together with an attribute.
zebralogic.example: Treating 'Peter lives in the first house' as merely an ordering hint and delaying the assignment, leading to ambiguous placements later.

zebralogic.title: Translate direct adjacency into offset constraints
zebralogic.principle: Clues that say 'X is directly left of Y' or 'directly right of Y' fix the two houses to be adjacent with a known direction. Encode them as position offsets (pos(Y) = pos(X) + 1 or -1).
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue uses the words 'directly left of' or 'directly right of'.
zebralogic.example: Interpreting 'X is directly left of Y' as merely 'X is somewhere left of Y', which loses the adjacency information.

zebralogic.title: Interpret distance clues correctly
zebralogic.principle: A clue stating 'N houses between X and Y' means there are exactly N houses separating them, so the absolute difference of their positions is N + 1. Do not confuse the number of houses with the distance itself.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue mentions a specific number of houses between two items.
zebralogic.example: Reading 'one house between X and Y' as 'X and Y are adjacent', which violates the intended spacing.

zebralogic.title: Bind equivalence clues to the same house
zebralogic.principle: If a clue equates two (or more) attribute values, they must occupy the same house. Treat the linked values as a single composite entity and propagate any other constraints attached to any member of the group.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue uses language like 'the person who ... is also the person who ...' or 'X equals Y'.
zebralogic.example: Assigning the same attribute (e.g., a sport) to two different houses because the equivalence with another attribute was ignored.

zebralogic.title: Treat 'somewhere left/right of' as inequality
zebralogic.principle: Clues that say 'X is somewhere to the left of Y' only impose an ordering (pos(X) < pos(Y)) without specifying adjacency. Record the inequality and keep both positions open for later refinement.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue uses the phrase 'somewhere left of' or 'somewhere right of'.
zebralogic.example: Treating 'X is somewhere left of Y' as 'X is directly left of Y', which incorrectly forces adjacency.

zebralogic.title: Apply exclusion constraints
zebralogic.principle: If a clue forbids an attribute from a particular house (e.g., 'X is not in the fifth house'), record that prohibition and never place that attribute there. This eliminates impossible placements early.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue contains a negation such as 'not in house N' or 'cannot be ...'.
zebralogic.example: Placing the Google Pixel 6 in house 5 despite a clue stating it is not in the fifth house.

zebralogic.title: Enforce uniqueness across each attribute category
zebralogic.principle: Each value in a category must appear exactly once across all houses. After assigning a value, remove it from the candidate lists of the remaining houses to maintain the one‑per‑category rule.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Continuously, after any assignment or elimination.
zebralogic.example: Assigning the same phone model to two different houses, violating the uniqueness rule.

zebralogic.title: Disambiguate overlapping attribute values across categories
zebralogic.principle: When a word appears in more than one attribute category (e.g., a name that is also a brand), keep the categories separate and never confuse them. Treat each occurrence according to its declared category.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Whenever a term could belong to multiple categories.
zebralogic.example: Mistaking the 'Apple' phone model for the name 'Apple' and assigning it to the Name category.

zebralogic.title: Preserve original case of attribute values
zebralogic.principle: Output attribute values exactly as they appear in the problem statement, preserving capitalization, spacing, and punctuation. This ensures the answer matches the canonical form used by the verifier.
zebralogic.example: Writing 'Oneplus 9' instead of the required 'oneplus 9', causing a mismatch with the reference answer.

zebralogic.title: Interpret 'next to each other' as bidirectional adjacency
zebralogic.principle: Clues that say two entities are 'next to each other' mean they occupy adjacent houses, but the order is not specified. Encode them as a pair of houses with a distance of one, without assuming a direction.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue uses the phrase 'next to each other' or 'are next to each other'.
zebralogic.example: Assuming 'X is next to Y' implies X is left of Y, which can lead to a reversed placement.

zebralogic.description: Treating 'somewhere left of' as adjacency (directly left)
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model conflates ordering clues with adjacency, ignoring that the clue only provides a relative ordering without distance.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Apply the 'Treat 'somewhere left/right of' as inequality' skill; record only the ordering constraint and keep both positions flexible.

zebralogic.description: Interpreting 'N houses between' as distance N
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model mistakenly treats the number of intervening houses as the total distance, forgetting that the positions differ by N + 1.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Use the 'Interpret distance clues correctly' skill to convert 'N houses between' into a position difference of N + 1.

zebralogic.description: Ignoring equivalence clues that bind two attributes to the same house
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model treats linked attributes as independent, leading to contradictory assignments.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Apply the 'Bind equivalence clues to the same house' skill and propagate all constraints attached to any member of the equivalence group.

zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model places the same attribute value in multiple houses, often due to incomplete elimination after assignments.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Enforce the 'Enforce uniqueness across each attribute category' skill continuously, removing assigned values from other houses' candidate sets.

zebralogic.description: Assuming a fixed direction for 'next to each other' clues
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model interprets 'next to each other' as a directed adjacency (e.g., X left of Y) instead of a bidirectional relationship.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Use the 'Interpret 'next to each other' as bidirectional adjacency' skill, encoding the pair as adjacent without a preset order.
